name: Sawyer Hall
use: Residence hall, 131 students; Paul College learning communities on the second floor

facts.text: Dedicated October 20, 1951, as a women's dormitory and named for Elizabeth Coffin Sawyer, the first woman on the Board of Trustees (1925–1932).
Small co-ed hall of 131 students at 7 Garrison Avenue, near Holloway Commons and Paul College, mostly double rooms.
Accessibility listed as braille signage, roll-in building access and strobe alerts in some rooms; no elevator or A/C listed.

verdict: 1951 Colonial Revival hall with a white columned porch in the best location on campus; plain rooms, leaky showers, no A/C.
notes: Architect not given by the archives. No renovation found. Photos: symmetrical three-storey red-brick Colonial Revival-style front with white columned porch, Palladian-style window and pediment with oculus, behind lawn and trees. Licensed photo (2013): symmetrical three-storey brick front with a white pedimented central bay, oculus and columned porch; tidy, conventional Colonial Revival. A near-duplicate (Sawyer Hall, UNH 2.jpg) was skipped.
judgeNotes: Photo shows a well-composed symmetrical front.
